goodEvidenceLooksLike: A named senior executive owns the fraud-risk programme, its budget, unresolved exceptions and reporting to the governing body. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows names one accountable executive and decision rights; shows decisions, owners and due dates; shows escalation after 30 days overdue.
controlObjective: Give one senior executive explicit authority and accountability for fraud-risk decisions.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Fraud appears as a discrete registered risk with an owner, inherent and residual ratings, linked controls and a review cycle, inside the same register the governing body already uses. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows fraud is a discrete entry, not folded into general operational risk; shows owner, rating basis and linked controls; rating changes carry written justification.
exampleArtifacts: Enterprise risk register extract showing the fraud entry
Inherent and residual ratings with written rationale
controlObjective: Carry fraud risk as a named risk inside the organisation-wide risk and governance framework rather than as an informal concern.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A named forum receives a standard fraud report on a fixed cadence covering incidents, losses, control failures, overdue actions and trend commentary, with decisions minuted. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows consistent template across consecutive periods; quantifies incidents, losses and overdue actions rather than narrative only; minutes show decisions, owners and dates.
exampleArtifacts: Last two fraud reports on the standard template
Forum terms of reference naming the standing agenda item
controlObjective: Give leadership a predictable, evidence-based view of fraud exposure, incidents and control weaknesses.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Management designs and operates fraud controls; internal audit or another independent function periodically tests them and reports without assuming management responsibility. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows separates operation from testing for each key control; gives assurance unrestricted reporting access; records conflicts and recusals.
exampleArtifacts: Internal audit charter or assurance mandate
likelyEvidenceOwner: Head of Risk and business control owners
controlObjective: Separate management ownership of fraud risk from independent assurance over that ownership.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Approved, version-controlled fraud policy and supporting procedures define prohibited conduct, prevention and detection duties, reporting routes, investigation handling and consequences, and reach the full workforce. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows version-controlled with named owner and review date; states consequences and reporting routes explicitly; reaches the full workforce including non-desk and contract staff.
exampleArtifacts: Approved fraud policy with version and approval date
controlObjective: Put the organisation’s fraud rules in writing so expected behaviour and required process are not left to individual interpretation.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Threat information is gathered from named sources, filtered for relevance to the operating model, and presented to leadership with an explicit implication for existing controls. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows cites dated external sources rather than general commentary; links each threat to a named process, channel or control; records an action or an explicit accept decision.
exampleArtifacts: Threat briefing papers presented to leadership
Relevance assessment mapping threats to existing controls
controlObjective: Keep leadership informed of fraud threats actually emerging in the sector, operating model and counterparty base.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A structured fraud risk assessment completed within the past two years covers the material processes, uses a repeatable method, rates inherent and residual risk, names owners and produces a tracked treatment plan. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows completed within the last 24 months; covers the material process population rather than a sample of convenience; every unacceptable residual risk has a named owner and due date.
exampleArtifacts: Approved treatment plan with owners and due dates
controlObjective: Establish a current, structured and documented view of where the organisation is actually exposed to fraud.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Each material process — procurement, payments, refunds, claims, stock, supplier management and service delivery as applicable — has documented fraud scenarios, the roles able to execute them, and the controls relied upon. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows names specific processes rather than functions; identifies the roles and permissions able to execute each scenario; signed by the accountable process owner.
exampleArtifacts: Process inventory identifying material value-bearing processes
Control linkage showing preventive and detective controls
likelyEvidenceOwner: Head of Risk with named process owners
controlObjective: Map fraud risk to the specific operational processes where value can actually be diverted.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Change governance includes a mandatory fraud-risk assessment step with defined triggers, a competent reviewer and a documented decision closed before implementation. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows trigger criteria are written and objective; review predates implementation; shows decision, reviewer and any accepted residual risk.
exampleArtifacts: Change process documentation showing the fraud gate and triggers
Completed fraud reviews for recent qualifying changes
Evidence the gate blocked or released go-live
controlObjective: Force a fraud-risk review into the design of new systems, channels, products, services and operational changes before they go live.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Defined business-change triggers require a fraud-risk refresh, with refreshed scenarios and control expectations recorded against the changed operating model. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows triggers are objective and cover outsourcing and channel change; refresh is traceable to a specific dated change; resulting gaps carry owners and due dates.
exampleArtifacts: Refresh records linked to specific change events
controlObjective: Keep the fraud risk picture aligned to how the organisation currently operates rather than how it operated when the assessment was written.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Third-party fraud scenarios are assessed by relationship type and risk tier, covering collusion, substitution, over-billing, impersonation and misuse of delegated authority, with controls mapped per tier. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers the complete third-party population including contractors and intermediaries; addresses delegated authority and system access explicitly; links each tier to named controls.
exampleArtifacts: Third-party inventory with relationship type and risk tier
Residual gaps recorded in the treatment plan
controlObjective: Assess the fraud risk introduced by suppliers, contractors, agents, intermediaries and other third parties acting for or with the organisation.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Named sources are monitored on a defined rhythm, relevance is assessed against the organisation’s processes and channels, and material threats generate a control review or an explicit accept decision. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows sources are specific and dated rather than generic media scanning; relevance assessed against named internal processes; every material threat has a decision and owner.
exampleArtifacts: Named source list with assigned responsibility
Relevance assessment against processes and channels
Control reviews or accept decisions arising
likelyEvidenceOwner: Fraud risk analyst or nominated owner
controlObjective: Track fraud threats emerging in the organisation’s own industry, geography and operating environment and convert them into control questions.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Insider fraud scenarios are assessed explicitly, including approval-limit abuse, permission accumulation, override use and collusion between roles, with compensating controls identified where separation is not achievable. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows names realistic role combinations rather than abstract insider risk; addresses override and emergency access explicitly; states the compensating control and its operator where separation fails.
exampleArtifacts: Documented compensating controls where separation is not possible
controlObjective: Consider deliberately how insiders could misuse authority, privileged access, approvals, system permissions or process gaps.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Each digital channel in use — portals, online forms, messaging journeys, loyalty programmes and service platforms — is assessed for enrolment, transaction, data-change and benefit-abuse fraud, with controls mapped per channel. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers every channel actually in use, including messaging journeys; distinguishes enrolment, transaction, data-change and benefit-abuse risk; links each risk to a named control.
exampleArtifacts: Control mapping for enrolment, transaction, data change and benefit abuse
Residual gaps in the treatment plan
controlObjective: Assess fraud risk arising through customer and user digital channels where the organisation operates them.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: High-risk processes have documented separation between initiation, approval, processing and reconciliation, enforced in system roles, with named compensating controls wherever headcount prevents full separation. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows maps all four duties for each in-scope process; tested against actual user entitlements, not intended design; compensating controls name the independent reviewer.
exampleArtifacts: System role configuration showing incompatible-duty blocks
Approved compensating controls where separation is not achievable
controlObjective: Ensure no single person can initiate, approve, process and reconcile the same high-risk transaction.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Written thresholds define which transactions require secondary approval, the approver is independent of the initiator, and the control is enforced systemically rather than by convention. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows thresholds are written and current; approver independence is demonstrable from system records; split-transaction analysis covers the complete population.
controlObjective: Require genuinely independent review or approval for transactions and activities above defined risk or value thresholds.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Every supplier is verified against legal identity, ownership, tax/banking and risk indicators before activation, with enhanced review for high-risk suppliers. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers the full supplier population added in the period; evidence predates activation; reviewer is different from requester.
controlObjective: Prevent fictitious, conflicted or misrepresented suppliers from entering the approved vendor population.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: All in-scope user access maps to an approved role, is reviewed by the business owner each quarter and is removed promptly after role change or exit. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows reconciles to the complete active-user population; shows reviewer, decision and date per entitlement; includes closure evidence for removals.
controlObjective: Keep ordinary system and data access aligned to current job responsibilities.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Refunds, credits, write-offs, stock adjustments, manual journals and overrides are captured completely, require documented reason codes, and are reviewed independently against the full population. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows population reconciles to system control totals; reviewer is outside the originating team; shows both threshold-based and sample-based coverage.
controlObjective: Bring sensitive manual adjustments under independent review because they bypass normal transactional controls.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Material processes are reviewed on a defined cycle against how they actually operate, with weaknesses logged, owned and tracked to closure. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows reviews the process as performed, not only as documented; includes transaction-level testing; weaknesses tracked to evidenced closure.
exampleArtifacts: Process review schedule and coverage plan
Completed review reports with walkthrough evidence
Weakness log with owners and due dates
likelyEvidenceOwner: Head of Risk with process owners
controlObjective: Periodically re-examine operational processes for control weaknesses and manipulation opportunities that have emerged in practice.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: High-risk roles are identified explicitly and subject to defined compensating measures such as secondary review, rotation, mandatory leave or enhanced monitoring, applied consistently and fairly. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows role list derived from authority, access and custody; shows the measure actually operated, not only assigned; applied consistently across comparable roles.
exampleArtifacts: Defined high-risk role list with rationale
controlObjective: Apply proportionate oversight to roles whose authority, access or custody creates elevated fraud opportunity.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Defined monitoring covers the material transaction and activity population, uses risk-based indicators, and produces reviewable output on a set rhythm rather than relying on incidental discovery. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows runs against the complete population, not a convenience sample; indicators map to identified fraud scenarios; output is routed to a named reviewer.
exampleArtifacts: Coverage report against process fraud maps
controlObjective: Actively monitor transactions and operational activity for unusual patterns, anomalies and red flags.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: The complete alert population is assigned, triaged to risk-based SLAs, dispositioned with evidence and independently reviewed for ageing and quality. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows shows completeness reconciliation; records reviewer, timestamps and rationale; separates closure-quality reviewer from alert investigator.
controlObjective: Ensure generated fraud and control exceptions are actually investigated and resolved.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A maintained catalogue of rules and data checks maps each test to a fraud scenario, runs against reconciled data, and is tuned from confirmed outcomes. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows each rule states scenario, source, threshold and reviewer; results reconcile to source system totals; tuning decisions are evidence-based.
exampleArtifacts: Rule and data-check catalogue with scenario linkage
Monthly tuning record with true/false positive outcomes
controlObjective: Use analytics, rules, reports or data checks to surface suspicious transactions, behaviour and control exceptions.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Defined triggers require detection rules and indicators to be reassessed, with changes recorded, tested before deployment and reported to the fraud forum. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows changes traceable to a dated trigger; tested before deployment; version history retained.
exampleArtifacts: Change triggers and rule version history
Pre-deployment test results against historical data
Coverage reporting to the fraud forum
controlObjective: Keep detection controls current as fraud methods, risks and operations change.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Monitoring explicitly addresses employee and insider misuse alongside external attack, with indicators, data sources and reviewers defined for both. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows separates internal and external indicators explicitly; covers every material process; gaps carry named owners and due dates.
exampleArtifacts: Indicator definitions for both threat classes
Coverage report to the fraud forum
controlObjective: Cover both internal misuse and external fraud threats within the monitoring design.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Written escalation criteria, routes and timeframes are defined, staff are trained on them, and escalation can bypass any implicated line manager. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows states criteria, recipient and timeframe explicitly; provides a conflict-free alternate route; timeliness measured against the stated criteria.
exampleArtifacts: Evidence of alternate route bypassing implicated management
controlObjective: Ensure monitoring staff know when to escalate and hold the authority to do so without obstruction.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A reviewer independent of the monitoring team periodically evaluates detection coverage, output quality and closure integrity, and reports findings to governance. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows reviewer is independent of the monitoring team; includes retesting of closed alerts, not only design review; findings tracked to evidenced closure.
exampleArtifacts: Coverage assessment against process fraud maps
controlObjective: Independently test whether detection controls are actually working, not merely running.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A documented plan defines intake, severity, command roles, containment, legal/evidence decisions, communications and closure, and is rehearsed annually. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows names commander, deputies and severity triggers; timestamps decisions and assigned actions; shows tabletop findings closed.
controlObjective: Create a repeatable, coordinated response to suspected fraud.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Reporting routes are published in plain language, reach the entire workforce including non-desk and contract staff, and awareness is periodically tested rather than assumed. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows reaches the full workforce, not only email users; states more than one route including a conflict-free option; awareness measured rather than assumed.
exampleArtifacts: Distribution evidence covering non-desk and contract staff
Targeted re-communication records where results were low
controlObjective: Make sure every employee knows exactly where and how to report suspected fraud or misconduct.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A written matrix assigns decision rights for triage severity, investigation authorisation, disciplinary and legal referral, recovery and closure, with conflict rules and deputies named. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers triage through closure, not investigation alone; names deputies for every decision; case records show who decided and why.
exampleArtifacts: Case files showing decisions with date and rationale
controlObjective: Define who decides what at each stage of fraud triage, investigation, escalation and closure.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Written investigation procedures govern confidentiality, subject fairness, interview conduct, documentation standards and legal privilege considerations, and investigators are competent to apply them. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows addresses confidentiality and subject fairness explicitly; documentation is contemporaneous and dated; closure review performed against the written procedure.
controlObjective: Conduct investigations so that confidentiality, fairness and documentary integrity are protected throughout.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Evidence is collected under legal direction where needed, hashed or sealed, logged through every transfer, access-restricted and retained under an approved schedule. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows unique evidence identifier on every item; unbroken timestamped custody trail; hash or seal reconciles at handover.
controlObjective: Identify, preserve and account for fraud evidence so integrity and provenance can be demonstrated.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Criteria define when external specialists are engaged, pre-qualified providers are identified in advance, and engagement terms protect confidentiality, privilege and evidential integrity. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows triggers are objective and assessed at triage; providers pre-qualified before an incident, not during one; terms address privilege, confidentiality and evidence handling.
exampleArtifacts: Pre-qualified provider list with agreed terms
Engagement or non-engagement decision per qualifying case
controlObjective: Bring in specialist forensic, legal, cyber or investigative capability when a case exceeds internal capability.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Every material incident produces a documented root-cause review with control actions, owners and due dates, tracked to evidenced closure and verified for effect. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows identifies control failure, not only individual culpability; actions carry named owners and due dates; verification confirms the control now operates.
exampleArtifacts: Root-cause analysis identifying failed or absent controls
Remediation register entries with owners and due dates
controlObjective: Convert what each incident reveals into control improvements that reduce repeat exposure.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A confidential and, where lawful, anonymous channel is continuously available, independently administered, access-restricted and protected by anti-retaliation escalation. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows supports confidential and anonymous intake; shows restricted identities and conflict routing; tracks acknowledgement and ageing.
controlObjective: Provide a safe, confidential route for internal and relevant external fraud concerns.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Channel instructions are published in the languages and formats the workforce uses, explain what happens after a report, and awareness and usability are periodically tested. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows explains anonymity and expected feedback; available in the languages and formats staff actually use; live test confirms intake through to case creation.
exampleArtifacts: Published channel instructions in relevant languages and formats
Follow-up communication where awareness was low
controlObjective: Ensure the workforce actually knows how to use the confidential reporting channel, not merely that one exists.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Triage routing rules automatically divert cases away from implicated individuals and their reporting lines, with an independent escalation route for reports naming senior management. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows excludes implicated parties and their reporting line; provides a route independent of executive management; access to case data is restricted and logged.
exampleArtifacts: Role-based case access list and access logs
Evidence of the alternate route for executive-level reports
controlObjective: Guarantee that reports are assessed independently of the people or teams they implicate.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A communicated anti-retaliation position is backed by monitoring of reporters’ employment outcomes, a route to raise retaliation concerns, and enforced consequences. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers contractors as well as employees; outcome monitoring is active rather than complaint-driven; substantiated retaliation results in recorded consequences.
controlObjective: State and enforce that retaliation against people who raise concerns is prohibited.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Where suppliers, contractors, customers or beneficiaries are relevant, the channel is externally reachable, publicised to them, and handles external reports under the same independence rules. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows reachable without internal network access or credentials; communicated to the relevant external population; external reports triaged under the same conflict rules.
exampleArtifacts: Supplier contract or onboarding references to the channel
Triage records applying the same independence rules
controlObjective: Extend reporting access to external stakeholders who observe misconduct the workforce cannot see.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Guidance and training describe observable indicators relevant to the organisation’s roles and settings, set the threshold for reporting suspicion rather than proof, and are refreshed with real anonymised cases. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows indicators are observable and role-relevant, not abstract; states clearly that proof is not required to report; refreshed using real anonymised cases.
exampleArtifacts: Guidance and training content showing observable indicators
likelyEvidenceOwner: Learning and Development with Ethics lead
controlObjective: Equip employees to recognise the behavioural and situational signals that should prompt a report.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: All third parties receive proportionate identity, ownership, sanctions/conflict and capability checks before contracting, with enhanced approval for high-risk relationships. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows evidence predates engagement; uses independent source data; documents match resolution and approver.
controlObjective: Risk-screen every supplier, contractor or third party before engagement.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Sourcing above defined thresholds follows a documented competitive process with sealed submissions, evaluation by a panel against pre-set criteria, conflict declarations and independent review of single-source awards. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows criteria demonstrably pre-date bid opening; panel evaluation with declared conflicts, not a single evaluator; pattern analysis covers the complete award population.
exampleArtifacts: Pre-set evaluation criteria dated before submission opening
Panel conflict declarations and scoring sheets
controlObjective: Protect competitive sourcing from collusion, manipulation, bid rigging and favouritism.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Declarations are collected from all staff able to influence supplier selection or payment, refreshed periodically and on change, tested against supplier data, and each declared conflict carries a documented management action. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers all roles able to influence selection or payment; includes proactive data matching, not declaration alone; each conflict has an applied and evidenced management action.
exampleArtifacts: Declaration register covering all in-scope roles
Data-matching results against the vendor master
Evidence of recusal or enhanced review being applied
controlObjective: Surface and actively manage employee conflicts of interest involving suppliers and third parties.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Every bank-detail change is verified independently through a trusted pre-existing contact and segregated from payment approval; invoices are matched to approved supplier and purchasing records. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows callback number predates the request; requester, verifier and approver are separated; covers the complete bank-change population.
exampleArtifacts: Pre-existing contact record and callback log
controlObjective: Prevent invoice manipulation and fraudulent vendor bank-detail changes before payment release.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: High-risk third parties are re-screened and performance-reviewed on a risk-based cycle covering ownership change, sanctions status, delivery performance, pricing drift and spend concentration. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers the complete high-risk population; includes re-screening, not performance review alone; findings tracked to evidenced action.
exampleArtifacts: Re-screening results for ownership and sanctions
controlObjective: Keep high-risk third-party relationships under periodic review after onboarding, not only at the point of engagement.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: An independent function periodically reviews procurement and vendor-master activity covering master-data changes, award patterns, spend outside contract and policy exceptions. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows reviewer independent of procurement and finance operations; covers vendor-master changes and award patterns by individual; findings tracked to evidenced closure.
exampleArtifacts: Award and exception pattern analysis by individual
controlObjective: Subject procurement and vendor-management activity itself to oversight, since it controls both supplier selection and payment eligibility.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Intermediary and outsourced arrangements carry contractual fraud-control obligations, audit and information rights, defined oversight of delegated authority, and periodic assurance over the provider’s own controls. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows contract states audit rights and authority limits explicitly; reconciliation covers the complete delegated transaction population; sub-contracting requires prior approval.
exampleArtifacts: Contract clauses covering fraud controls, audit rights and delegated authority limits
Reconciliation of intermediary-handled transactions or collections
controlObjective: Address the specific fraud risks created by agents, brokers, distributors, intermediaries and outsourced providers acting on the organisation’s behalf.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Identity verification is applied at defined risk points using independent sources proportionate to risk, with results recorded, exceptions approved and re-verification on sensitive change. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows uses independent sources rather than self-supplied documents alone; verification predates activation or first payment; retention respects applicable data-protection obligations.
exampleArtifacts: Defined verification risk points and required checks
Verification records with source and date
likelyEvidenceOwner: Process owners for onboarding and activation
controlObjective: Verify the identity of customers, users, employees, suppliers and counterparties wherever identity misuse could create loss or harm.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Risk-based monitoring covers material digital events, alerts are triaged to defined SLAs and rules are tuned from confirmed outcomes. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows reconciles monitored events to source feeds; maps each rule to a risk and sla; records evidence-based disposition.
controlObjective: Detect suspicious login, account, access and transaction behaviour on digital platforms.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Training is role-relevant, reinforced by periodic simulations, measured by behaviour rather than completion alone, and supported by a fast reporting route with feedback. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows targets high-risk roles specifically; measures report rate, not completion alone; links to an out-of-band verification requirement.
exampleArtifacts: Role-relevant training content and completion records
Simulation results including click and report rates
Verification procedure for payment and bank-detail instructions
controlObjective: Prepare employees to recognise and resist phishing, social engineering and digital impersonation.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Every privileged account is named, justified, least-privileged, strongly authenticated, logged and independently recertified quarterly; emergency access expires automatically. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers human, service, shared and emergency accounts; separates reviewer from account administrator; shows owner, decision, date and closure.
controlObjective: Restrict and independently recertify privileged, administrator and sensitive-data access.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Monitoring joins user, transaction and change events across material digital channels, with risk-based triage and retained investigation evidence. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows maps scenarios to events and thresholds; proves source-feed completeness; records analyst rationale and escalation.
controlObjective: Detect misuse, unauthorised transactions, suspicious data changes and digital-channel abuse.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Reporting routes are published for both staff and external users, monitored during defined hours with defined response times, and feed directly into monitoring and incident response. Good evidence identifies the accountable owner and shows covers both internal staff and external users where relevant; states monitored hours and response targets; demonstrates connection to incident response.
exampleArtifacts: Published reporting routes for staff and users
Evidence reports feed into triage and incident response
controlObjective: Give employees and users a fast, known route to report suspicious digital activity or account-security concerns.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Digital threat review runs on a defined cycle covering channel-specific attack methods, assesses them against current controls, and produces owned actions or explicit accept decisions. exampleArtifacts: Digital threat review records with sources
Action log with owners and due dates

controlObjective: Periodically reassess emerging digital fraud risks relevant to the organisation’s operations and sector.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Sufficient logging, alerting and investigative capability exists to identify compromise, reconstruct what occurred, contain it and support recovery or referral. exampleArtifacts: Log coverage inventory for identity-bearing systems

Investigation runbook and a worked case example
controlObjective: Be able to detect and investigate identity misuse, account takeover, impersonation and unauthorised profile changes.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Role-based fraud learning is completed at induction and annually, refreshed for emerging risks and tested for understanding and behaviour. controlObjective: Equip staff to recognise and act on fraud risks specific to their roles.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Induction includes fraud content covering policy, reporting routes, consequences and role-relevant risks, is completed within a defined period of joining, and covers contractors where they hold equivalent access. controlObjective: Establish fraud expectations at the point of joining, before habits and local practice form.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Leaders communicate expectations on a defined rhythm through visible channels, model them in decisions, and reinforce that results never justify control bypass. exampleArtifacts: Leadership communication records with dates and reach

controlObjective: Have leadership set explicit, repeated expectations on ethical conduct, conflicts and fraud prevention.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Consequences are documented in policy and employment terms, applied consistently regardless of seniority, and communicated through anonymised outcomes so deterrence is credible. controlObjective: Ensure employees understand the actual consequences of fraudulent, dishonest or unethical behaviour.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: Awareness material uses anonymised real cases and realistic scenarios drawn from the organisation’s own processes and sector, refreshed as methods change. controlObjective: Use real examples, scenarios and lessons learned so staff recognise fraud as it actually presents.

controlObjective: Build genuine confidence that raising a concern is safe and will be taken seriously.

controlObjective: Periodically re-examine the fraud risk profile and the control environment as a whole rather than only at incident time.

goodEvidenceLooksLike: A structured root-cause method is applied to material incidents and near-misses, distinguishing design failure, operating failure and absent control, with themes aggregated across cases. controlObjective: Translate lessons from investigations and incidents into actual changes in controls, process, training or monitoring.

controlObjective: Monitor fraud trends affecting the organisation’s sector, geography, customer environment and supplier base.
